root_cause.text: The OMAP GPIO driver incorrectly registered the `omap_mpuio_driver` from `omap_gpio_probe()` via `omap_mpuio_init()`, i.e. while a device lock was already held, which violates driver-core locking rules and can deadlock, and it also left the subdriver unregistered on module unload.
root_cause.evidence: The patch says `omap_mpuio_init()` was “called from omap_gpio_probe()” and originally did `platform_driver_register(&omap_mpuio_driver)` there; the fix moves `platform_driver_register(&omap_mpuio_driver)` to `omap_gpio_drv_reg()` (module initcall) and adds `platform_driver_unregister(&omap_mpuio_driver)` in `omap_gpio_exit()`, explicitly noting that “the driver core does not allow registering drivers with a device lock already being held” and that this led to a “potential deadlock condition.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Register the MPU I/O platform device only once while preserving driver data updates on initialization.
intent_record.what: The function omap_mpuio_init() was changed to introduce a static bool registered flag, keep the platform_set_drvdata() call, and replace the conditional platform_driver_register() check with an unconditional first-time-only platform_device_register() call guarded by registered.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the MPU I/O platform device is now registered only once per process lifetime instead of attempting registration each time omap_mpuio_init() runs. This avoids repeated device registration attempts while still updating the device's drvdata to point at the current gpio_bank.

intent_record.intent_summary: Register and clean up the MPU IO platform driver together with the GPIO driver, with rollback on init failure.
intent_record.what: The init function was changed from directly registering only `omap_gpio_driver` to first registering `omap_mpuio_driver`, then registering `omap_gpio_driver`, and unregistering `omap_mpuio_driver` if the second registration fails. The exit function was also updated to unregister `omap_mpuio_driver` in addition to `omap_gpio_driver`.
intent_record.how: At runtime, both platform drivers are now brought up during initialization, ensuring the MPU IO driver is available alongside the GPIO driver. If GPIO driver registration fails, the previously registered MPU IO driver is cleaned up to avoid leaving partial state behind. On module exit, both drivers are properly removed, preventing a stale driver from remaining registered.

candidates.rationale: This registers the omap_mpuio_driver from omap_mpuio_init(), which is invoked during GPIO probe while a device lock is already held. That violates driver-core locking rules and can deadlock; it is also the registration path that was not properly paired with unload cleanup.

This follows the driver registration inside omap_mpuio_init() and contributes to creating the subdevice/driver binding from within the locked probe path, which is part of the unsafe registration sequence described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This is the driver-core registration of omap_mpuio_driver from omap_mpuio_init(), which was invoked during omap_gpio_probe() while a device lock was already held, creating the deadlock-prone and improperly paired registration sequence described in the root cause.

This registers the companion MPU I/O platform device as part of the same unsafe init path, contributing to the subdriver binding being created from within the locked probe context and leaving the registration lifecycle incorrect on unload.
